run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

The only application error in the whole telemetry set is one search->rate gRPC call: in trace 77d2a7e08d07a9f4 at 06:24:34.7Z, search's client span /rate.Rate/GetRates was recorded error=true / otel.status_code=ERROR at 1,000,725us - the search Deployment's RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS=1000 deadline - because rate's /rate.Rate/GetRates span (1,021,239us) was consumed by a mongo_rate client span of 1,020,667us; search retried and the retry was served from memcached in 253us, and the enclosing frontend HTTP GET /hotels still returned 200 in 1,108,895us. Steady state afterwards is healthy (at 06:26:11Z, GET /hotels 1.87-3.29 ms all HTTP 200; rate GetRates 12-396us from memcached; geo/profile/reservation/user/recommendation spans all sub-millisecond or low-millisecond with no error status). Separately, the wrk2 load generator targeting the frontend Service reports 186-187 client-side socket timeouts per 30 s round (2934 requests in 30.03 s, ~98 req/s) while completed requests stay at p50 2.1 ms / max 7.2 ms; no frontend span >=800 ms, no error-status span and no error log correspond to those requests (frontend error count is 0), so that stall class remains unattributed. Because the 1.02 s MongoDB latency in the rate service was seen exactly once and no baseline or time series exists, the database-latency explanation is a partially supported hypothesis, not a proven sustained fault.

At 2026-11-25T06:26:12Z the only container in hotel-reservation with kube_pod_container_status_ready == 0 is the container 'archiver' of pod audit-log-archiver-29926465-gxmzf (container 'fluent-bit-sidecar' of that pod and every hotel-reservation application container are ready); that pod's own logs show the archive record forwarded and 'upload complete', so it is outside the hotel-reservation request path.

In trace 77d2a7e08d07a9f4 (frontend request started 2026-11-25T06:24:34.705Z) the frontend server span 'HTTP GET /hotels' lasted 1,108,895us with http.status_code=200, and inside it the search client span '/rate.Rate/GetRates' carried error=true and otel.status_code=ERROR with duration 1,000,725us; a second '/rate.Rate/GetRates' call in the same trace (570us client, 253us rate server span) then succeeded.

In the same trace the rate service's server span '/rate.Rate/GetRates' (service_name=rate) lasted 1,021,239us and its child client span 'mongo_rate' lasted 1,020,667us, while the four other 'mongo_rate' spans in that call were only 6,164-7,833us, so the latency of that call originates in the rate service's MongoDB access.

The search Deployment's container env sets RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS=1000, RATE_RPC_MAX_ATTEMPTS=2, RATE_RPC_INITIAL_BACKOFF_MS=100, RATE_RPC_BACKOFF_MULTIPLIER=2.0 and RATE_RPC_JITTER=0.2; the failing client span duration of 1,000,725us matches that 1000 ms deadline.
The rate Deployment's container env sets RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT=500 and RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY=256 (no other hotel-reservation service has rate-limit or queue settings).

Span counters at 06:26:12Z: search '/rate.Rate/GetRates' 2267 STATUS_CODE_UNSET + 1 STATUS_CODE_ERROR; rate '/rate.Rate/GetRates' 2314 server spans with memcached_get_multi_rate 2314 and mongo_rate only 64; frontend 'HTTP GET /hotels' 2265, 'HTTP GET /recommendations' 1506, 'HTTP POST /reservation' 24, 'HTTP POST /user' 19, all STATUS_CODE_UNSET; rate received 46 more GetRates server spans than search has successful client spans.

In steady state at 2026-11-25T06:26:11Z, 10 frontend 'HTTP GET /hotels' spans lasted 1,866-3,294us with http.status_code=200; rate '/rate.Rate/GetRates' server spans 12-396us served through memcached_get_multi_rate with no mongo_rate child spans; geo 30-172us; profile 11-219us; reservation 20-482us; user 7-16us; none carried an error status.

The load generator pod wrk2-job-mdj86 (pod no longer present) ran 30 s rounds against http://10.96.169.158:5000, the frontend ClusterIP Service: '2934 requests in 30.03s, 1.18MB read', 'Requests/sec: 97.72', 'Socket errors: connect 0, read 0, write 0, timeout 187', with recorded latency p50 2.13 ms, p99 5.05 ms and max 7.16 ms; consecutive rounds reported timeout 187, 187 and 186.

A Loki scan of hotel-reservation for '(?i)(error|fail|denied|not authorized|panic|timeout)' over 05:26:12-06:26:12Z returned 25 lines, all of them wrk2 socket-timeout summaries, frontend 'consul ... connection refused' lines at 06:24:20-06:24:23Z (before consul was ready), consul election warnings and mongodb startup/session warnings - no application-level error or 'not authorized' line.

mongodb-rate mounts ConfigMap failure-admin-rate at /scripts (scripts revoke-admin-rate-mongo.sh / remove-mitigate-admin-rate-mongo.sh / revoke-mitigate-admin-rate-mongo.sh operate on the 'rate-db' admin user), yet mongodb-rate's logs for 06:24:00-06:26:12Z contain only WiredTiger open/recovery/checkpoint messages (last checkpoint 06:25:26.882Z) and no authentication or authorization failure.

Every hotel-reservation Service has exactly one ready endpoint address on the expected port (e.g. frontend 10.96.169.158 -> 10.244.234.136:5000, rate -> 10.244.234.141:8084, search -> 10.244.234.143:8082, mongodb-rate -> 10.244.7.205:27017) with no notReadyAddresses, and all 6 PVCs (geo-pvc, profile-pvc, rate-pvc, recommendation-pvc, reservation-pvc, user-pvc) are Bound at 1Gi.
All four nodes (sregym-control-plane, sregym-worker, sregym-worker2, sregym-worker3) report condition Ready=true and no MemoryPressure, DiskPressure or PIDPressure condition is true at 06:26:12Z.

Prometheus holds only a single sample of traces_span_metrics_calls_total in the window: a whole-window range query of sum(traces_span_metrics_calls_total) returned exactly one point (value 43521 at 2026-11-25T06:26:12Z) and rate()/increase() over 30m returned 0 for every service, so the trace-derived counters are a point-in-time snapshot and no error-rate or latency trend can be computed from them.

The rate pod rate-65d6967c95-srbbh and the mongodb-rate pod mongodb-rate-56cc8659c9-vbhdc are Running and Ready with restartCount 0, and the normal rate request path is served from memcached in 12-396us with only 64 mongo_rate spans in total, so a general rate or mongodb-rate outage or sustained throttling is not supported by the data.

Revocation of the MongoDB admin user's readWrite role on rate-db (the mounted failure-admin-rate ConfigMap exists for exactly that) is rejected as the cause of the observed failure: the failing span is a client deadline exceeded (error=true, duration 1,000,725us), not an authorization error, mongodb-rate logs no authentication failure, and rate's mongo-backed queries immediately after startup completed in about 6 ms.

The 1.1 s frontend /hotels latency and the single search '/rate.Rate/GetRates' ERROR span are best explained by a transient ~1.02 s MongoDB round trip in the rate service's mongo_rate call at 06:24:34.7Z, which exceeded search's RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS=1000 deadline and was absorbed by a retry; because only one such sample exists, a sustained rate/mongodb-rate latency problem is not established.

The ~186-187 wrk2 socket timeouts per 30 s round form a separate, unattributed stall class: apart from the single 1.109 s trace, no frontend span >=800 ms exists in the retained Jaeger data and frontend error-status spans are 0, so the timed-out requests either never reached the frontend process or never completed a span; their cause (frontend request path, service network path, or load generator) cannot be decided from the available evidence.

search's retry/timeout settings (RATE_RPC_MAX_ATTEMPTS=2 with RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS=1000 and 100 ms initial backoff) act as an amplifier rather than the origin: rate recorded 2314 '/rate.Rate/GetRates' server spans against 2267 successful search client spans, consistent with duplicate calls after a deadline miss, and the 1,000,725us ERROR span sits exactly on the configured 1000 ms deadline.

Before treating the latency as a fault, collect a longer baseline for rate's mongo_rate latency and frontend p99: the whole namespace is only ~2 minutes old at the end of the window, and the trace-derived metrics give a single sample, so no trend or comparable pre-incident baseline exists.

Check storage/host latency for mongodb-rate's rate-pvc and correlate it with rate's mongo_rate spans, and if the DB p99 can legitimately exceed 1 s, review search's RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS and retry budget so a slow dependency does not become an ERROR plus duplicate load.

To attribute the wrk2 timeout class, capture per-request frontend server metrics (status and duration) and the load generator's timeout setting/script, and check the client-to-Service network path; the wrk2 Job pod and its command line no longer exist, so its timeout value could not be read.

gaps: No pre-incident baseline exists: every Deployment in hotel-reservation was created 2026-11-25T06:24:05-06:24:06Z and the pods 06:24:05-06:24:09Z, so the state before that rollout - and what triggered it - is unknown; the change_history integration is not available in this Run.

The trace-derived counters are a single point-in-time sample (one point at 06:26:12Z; rate()/increase() returned 0 and a 24h rate query returned nothing), so error-rate and latency trends cannot be computed; no application request/latency metrics exist in Prometheus besides traces_span_metrics_calls_total and kube-state-metrics series.

The 1,020,667us mongo_rate latency has no server-side MongoDB evidence: mongodb-rate logs contain no slow-query entry and mongo is not traced, so whether mongodb-rate storage was slow, or the delay was on the client/network side, cannot be determined; the cause rests on one occurrence only.

The 186-187 wrk2 socket timeouts per 30 s round cannot be attributed: no matching frontend span >=800 ms, no error-status span, and no application error log line exists, and the wrk2 Job pod and its command line (including its timeout value and script) no longer exist.
Jaeger keeps only a limited in-memory set of traces (most recent ~5000) and the query tool returns a projected sample, so a span or trace that was not returned is unknown, not absent.

Several Prometheus queries were not usable as evidence by design: the 24h rate over traces_span_metrics_calls_total returned no data and kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total > 0 returned no data, so absence of restarts is taken only from the pod/container objects and kube_pod_container_status_ready, not from the restart counter.

The audit-log-archiver container in pod audit-log-archiver-29926465-gxmzf shows ready=0 at 06:26:12Z; its logs show the record forwarded and upload complete, and it is outside the hotel-reservation request path, so its not-ready state was not pursued further.
next_steps: Collect a longer baseline (30+ minutes) of rate's mongo_rate latency, mongodb-rate host/PV latency and frontend p99 before confirming or dismissing a database-latency fault.

Compare the wrk2 timeout budget with observed latencies and inspect the frontend-to-Service network path (conntrack, kube-proxy, node CPU on sregym-worker2 where wrk2 ran) to explain the ~6% client timeouts.

Review the fault-injection style settings on the search Deployment (RATE_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS, RATE_RPC_MAX_ATTEMPTS, backoff) and on the rate Deployment (RATE_BACKEND_QPS_LIMIT, RATE_QUEUE_CAPACITY) against the intended production values, since these are the only non-default tunables in the namespace.

If authorization faults are suspected, verify the admin user's roles on rate-db and geo-db directly (note: the failure-admin-rate / failure-admin-geo scripts are mounted but no evidence of execution was found, and secrets cannot be read).

data.k8s-geo-mongo.sh:
#!/bin/bash


ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"

ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

TARGET_DB="geo-db"
READ_WRITE_ROLE="readWrite"

echo "Waiting for MongoDB to start..."
until mongo --eval "print('waited for connection')" > /dev/null 2>&1; do
  sleep 1
done
echo "MongoDB started"

# Create the admin user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating admin user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ADMIN_USER', pwd: '$ADMIN_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ADMIN_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ADMIN_USER -p $ADMIN_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

# Create the root user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating root user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ROOT_USER', pwd: '$ROOT_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database to root
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ROOT_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ROOT_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"


echo "Initialization script completed"
